Referral Note (intake, at wife's request)

Mr. Morrow, a 48-year-old married man, is seen for outpatient psychiatric evaluation at his wife's request. She describes about 18 months of increasing suspiciousness, centered on his workplace, where he has filed several complaints with management about coworkers. He believes several coworkers are intentionally trying to damage his reputation and steal his ideas, and he interprets ordinary workplace conversations as coded messages directed at him; management has found no supporting evidence for his complaints. He continues to work but has become socially isolated and increasingly distrustful, and has had growing conflict with colleagues. He states that he feels fine and is attending at his wife's urging. No previous psychiatric treatment. Type 2 diabetes, treated with metformin. Denies alcohol misuse or drug use. Referred for diagnostic evaluation and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Casually dressed; adequately groomed.

Behavior: Alert and fully oriented. Cooperative but guarded throughout the interview. Brought a folder of printed workplace emails, which he keeps closed on his lap.

Speech: Normal.

Mood / Affect: Mood "fine." Affect mildly constricted.

Thought / Perception: Thought processes organized. Thought content reveals fixed persecutory beliefs. No hallucinations or marked disorganization.

Cognition / Insight: Alert and fully oriented. Insight poor; judgment fair.
